claims.text: Cast AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic high-entropy alloys can exhibit coarse lamellar phases forming an in situ composite structure.
Tailored rolling and annealing can produce an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure while retaining inherited lamellar features.
The approach should be effective in eutectic high-entropy alloys that naturally develop lamellar structures.
The approach may not work in single-phase or non-eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Processing that eliminates the lamellar morphology will eliminate its beneficial effect.
The targeted structural mediator is an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure containing inherited lamellar composite regions.
Inherited duplex lamellar regions create a two-hierarchical constraint effect.
The inherited duplex lamellar microstructure enables a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism.
The refined duplex lamellar structure impedes dislocation motion.
The refined duplex lamellar structure deflects or arrests propagating microcracks.
The hierarchical microstructure enhances yield strength.
The hierarchical microstructure enhances Young's modulus.
The hierarchical microstructure preserves or improves ductility while increasing strength.
The hierarchical microstructure improves fracture resistance or fracture toughness.
Tailored processing is expected to increase yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to conventionally processed eutectic HEAs.
Tailored processing is expected to increase Young's modulus by approximately 20–30% relative to conventionally processed eutectic HEAs.
Tailored processing is expected to maintain or enhance ductility.
Tailored processing is expected to maintain or enhance fracture toughness.
Conventional thermo-mechanical processing produces a coarser microstructure with less effective microcrack arrest.
Conventionally processed eutectic HEAs have lower overall mechanical-property synergy than the proposed processed state.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis promises improvement in all four properties, whereas the predicted outcome only requires ductility and fracture toughness to be maintained or enhanced, allowing no improvement in those two properties.

The predicted outcome allows merely maintaining ductility and fracture toughness, but the falsification rule appears to require approximately 10% or greater enhancement in every property, imposing a stronger criterion than the stated prediction.
